clue.text: Visiting from abroad, tons jamming pub that’s full

indicators.note: to jam is to squeeze into a tight space, so one piece is pushed inside another

blocks.note: someone visiting is in, at the place
de is French for 'from', a foreign word for it
T is the abbreviation for tons
PH, public house, is the map abbreviation for a pub

explanation.surface: A tourist finds a packed pub, crammed with tons of drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: PH is the Ordnance Survey map abbreviation for a public house; T goes inside it to make PTH, after IN and the French DE.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-depth study is a thorough, comprehensive one, covering every detail rather than skimming.

clue.text: Crew covered by press in gruelling race

indicators.note: in a down entry, being covered by something puts that thing on top, so it comes first

blocks.note: to press clothes is to iron them
to crew a ship is to man it

explanation.surface: A team gets hounded by reporters during a punishing race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crew' and 'press' look like nouns (a team, journalists) but both are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ironman is a triathlon of long swim, bike ride and marathon, famously exhausting to complete.

clue.text: Easing of tensions as Harvey, jumping around, leaves three-day event freely

indicators.note: when someone leaves a place they are no longer in it, so those letters are taken out
the letters to go are scattered here and there rather than sitting together in one run
arranged freely means with no fixed order, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A horseman called Harvey quits an equestrian three-day event, calming nerves all round.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike H, A, R, V, E, Y from wherever they sit in THREE DAY EVENT, leaving T, E, E, D, E, N, T to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Détente is the diplomatic word for a relaxation of hostility between rival states, famously in the Cold War.

clue.text: Evidence in favour of Ofcom written up, oddly vanishing

indicators.note: if the odd-numbered letters vanish, only the even-numbered ones are left behind
in a down entry, writing upwards runs the letters bottom to top, turning them round

blocks.note: pro means for, in favour of
the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: Someone backing the broadcasting regulator finds their supporting documents mysteriously disappearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Ofcom is the UK's broadcasting and telecoms regulator; only its even letters F and O survive, then flip.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof is the evidence that establishes a claim as true, as in a court or in mathematics.

clue.text: Rash was at the front of hip to begin with

indicators.note: a thing that comes to begin with is placed first in the line

blocks.note: hip and hot both mean fashionable, in demand
to head a queue is to be at its front

explanation.surface: A skin rash that first appeared on someone's hip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like a skin complaint but is the adjective meaning reckless; 'hip' is not the body part but a word for trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotheaded person acts impetuously without thinking, which is exactly what being rash means.

clue.text: Hit uniform speed on short journey

indicators.note: something cut short is missing its end, so the last letter goes
one thing sitting on another in an across entry follows it

blocks.note: a trip is a journey; lose its last letter
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
miles per hour, the unit speed is measured in

explanation.surface: Someone clocks a regulation speed on a brief outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit' reads as a verb but is the noun, a success, as in a smash hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph is a great success or victory, just as a show or record that is a hit.

clue.text: Leaning right, nurse admits

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: to nurse the sick is to tend them
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A nurse confesses to being right-wing in politics.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'leaning right' as a political stance; the definition is just 'Leaning', a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend is a general tendency or inclination, a direction things lean towards over time.

clue.text: Reform is inane with party splitting country

indicators.note: to reform something is to form it anew, so these letters get a new arrangement
to split something is to drive into its middle, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A political reform is mocked as inane while a party divides the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reform' reads as a noun about policy but is the instruction to rearrange 'is inane'; 'party' sits inside that result.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is a large archipelago nation in Southeast Asia, one example of a country.

clue.text: Mighty America yielding to international report

indicators.note: to yield to someone is to give way and let them take your place

blocks.note: mighty and massive both mean huge
A is the abbreviation for America; it is the letter replaced
I is the abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: A powerful America bows to a global report.
explanation.walkthrough: In MASSIVE the A swaps out for I.
explanation.definitionFit: A missive is a written message or letter, loosely a report sent from one person to another.

clue.text: Makes solid career collecting diamonds with turnover of tin

indicators.note: to collect something is to take it in, so one piece is held inside
turning something over flips it, so the letters run backwards
with means alongside, so the next piece is simply added on

blocks.note: to career is to rush headlong, to hare
D is the abbreviation for the card suit diamonds
Sn is the chemical symbol for tin

explanation.surface: A solid career in mining gathers diamonds and does well from tin sales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like a noun about a job but is the verb, to rush; 'turnover' is not a business figure but a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To harden something is to make it firm or rigid, as setting concrete or cooling metal does.

clue.text: Withdraws hint for tops?

blocks.note: surface reading: a clue pointing to spinning toys or clothing tops
setter's reading: the answer, read as a clue itself, rearranges a four-letter word into the fodder for 'tops'

explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as a clue, with OPTS as fodder and OUT as the rearrangement signal, and it yields TOPS.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt out is to choose not to take part, so to withdraw from a scheme or arrangement.

clue.text: Customer‘s tip ahead of cycling trick

indicators.note: being ahead of something places it earlier in the line
going round a cycle moves the front letter round to the back

blocks.note: the tip of something is its end
a ruse is a trick or deception

explanation.surface: A shopper's tip is a trick for cycling ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', so 'Customer' alone is the definition; RUSE sends its R to the back to become USER.
explanation.definitionFit: The end user is the final consumer who actually uses a product, the customer at the end of the chain.

clue.text: Motor sport stops idle men moving around hazardous area

indicators.note: letters that move around change their positions, so they are rearranged
to stop a gap is to plug it, so one piece fills the middle of another

blocks.note: taken as written
Formula One, F1, with the digit 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A motor race is halted as idle spectators wander onto a dangerous part of the track.
explanation.walkthrough: F1 is Formula One; crosswords often read the digit 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A minefield is a stretch of ground laid with explosive mines, literally a dangerous zone.

clue.text: Row of ten heading west amongst other directions

indicators.note: in an across entry, going west means travelling right to left, so the letters run backwards
amongst means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside others

blocks.note: 10 written with the digit 1 as I and the zero as O
the compass points other than west: north, south, east

explanation.surface: A line of ten people heading west while others go in different directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a line but is the rhyme-with-cow sense, a din; the other directions are the compass points once west has been used.
explanation.definitionFit: A row, in the sense of a loud quarrel or racket, is a lot of noise.

clue.text: One in family dropping drug into cordial

indicators.note: dropping something into a thing puts it inside

blocks.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
cordial means friendly, pleasant

explanation.surface: A relative slips a drug into a fruit cordial drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cordial' looks like the fruit drink but is the adjective for warm and friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece, a sibling's daughter, is one relative among the members of a family.

clue.text: Function you reportedly had come about

indicators.note: a report passes on what was said, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a function is a social event
the letter U is said the same as this word
to have a meal is to eat it

explanation.surface: Someone is told that a party you threw actually happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' reads as a mathematical or working role but is a social occasion; 'had' is had to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: To eventuate is a formal verb meaning to happen or result, the same as to come about.

clue.text: Stride carelessly around highly trained men coming to blows

indicators.note: done carelessly, without order, so the letters are jumbled
one piece placed around another encloses it

blocks.note: taken as written
the SAS is the British Army's Special Air Service, an elite unit

explanation.surface: Soldiers marching sloppily around elite troops start fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming to blows' looks like a single phrase for fighting; 'coming to' is only the link, and 'blows' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Blows in the sense of setbacks or shocks are misfortunes, the plural nouns for calamities.

clue.text: Tough call to insert medical splint? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: inserting puts something inside another thing, one piece within a second
this flips the previous instruction, so the piece meant to go in becomes the outside one instead

blocks.note: a stent is a tube that holds a blood vessel open
to call someone on the phone is to ring them

explanation.surface: A doctor faces a hard decision about fitting a splint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite the opposite' flips the instruction: instead of STENT going into RING, RING goes into STENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringent rules are strict and demanding, so tough in the sense of severe.

clue.text: Exposed Musk lying about profligate support

indicators.note: something exposed has lost its outer covering, so the edge letters are stripped off
to lie about something is to lie around it, surrounding it

blocks.note: the inner letters of Musk
a profligate is a wasteful big spender

explanation.surface: Elon Musk is exposed lying about his extravagant backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' suggests dishonesty but here means lying physically, positioned around something.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspender is a strap or garter that holds up socks or stockings, a kind of support.

clue.text: Did some sport, taking two minutes and took top off

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside

blocks.note: skiing is a sport, so did some of it
M is the abbreviation for minute, twice

explanation.surface: An athlete trained for a couple of minutes and then took their shirt off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took top off' sounds like undressing but refers to removing cream from the top of milk.
explanation.definitionFit: To skim milk is to remove the cream that rises to the surface, so to take the top layer off.

clue.text: Triggers purists when swinging

indicators.note: something swinging moves about freely, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Traditionalists are provoked when something swings, as in jazz or swinging parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Triggers' reads as a noun but is the verb, sets off.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up trouble or feelings is to provoke or set them off, which is what triggering does.

clue.text: Courts having answer before hearing finishes prematurely

indicators.note: coming before something puts it earlier in the line
a thing finishing too soon stops before its final letter

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
a court hearing is a trial; drop its last letter

explanation.surface: Law courts where an answer comes before a hearing that ends early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courts' looks legal like 'hearing', but it means courtyards, open halls.
explanation.definitionFit: Atria, plural of atrium, are open central halls or courtyards in a building, so courts in the architectural sense.

clue.text: Looking embarrassed carrying tabloid around, with Sun’s initial best wishes

indicators.note: brought around means turned about, so the letters run backwards
to carry something is to hold it within
an initial is a first letter, so only the start is kept
with means alongside, so the next piece is simply added on

blocks.note: someone embarrassed goes red in the face
a rag is a disparaging word for a tabloid paper
the first letter of Sun

explanation.surface: Someone red-faced to be seen carrying the Sun tabloid around sends their best wishes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, which the surface uses to disguise that only its first letter is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Regards, as in a letter sign-off, are friendly greetings, the same sentiment as best wishes.

clue.text: Drawer left incomplete, held up by a new carpenter?

indicators.note: something left unfinished lacks its final part, so the last letter goes
in a down entry, a thing held up by another sits on top of it, so it comes first

blocks.note: someone who draws is an artist
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A drawer left half-built is propped up by a newly hired carpenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' looks like a piece of furniture, which fits the carpenter, but is one who draws; the question mark flags that a carpenter is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker, and a carpenter is one example of such a craftsman.

clue.text: Charlie‘s turn of phrase making Mike tense

indicators.note: to make one thing into another is to change it, so a letter is exchanged

blocks.note: an idiom is a turn of phrase
M is Mike in the NATO phonetic alphabet; it is the letter replaced
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Charlie's way with words puts his friend Mike on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: A Charlie is British slang for a fool; the 's is 'is'. Charlie and Mike both look like NATO alphabet letters, but only Mike is one here.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, a proper Charlie is a foolish person, a synonym for a nitwit or fool.

clue.text: Operating without preparation, guilt evens out after victory drink

indicators.note: with the even-numbered letters thrown out, only the odd ones remain
coming after something places it later in the line

blocks.note: a victory is a win
gin is an alcoholic drink
the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: An unprepared surgeon operates, their guilt levelling out after a celebratory drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evens out' looks like levelling off, but it removes the even-numbered letters of 'guilt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Winging it is an idiom for improvising, doing something without rehearsal or planning.

clue.text: Club with upper hand

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
having the edge means having the advantage

explanation.surface: A club where the members hold the advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' suggests a society holding the advantage, but it is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedge is a golf club with a steeply angled face, used for short, high shots.

clue.text: Inspire Kemi’s possible statement of political allegiance, ignoring Liberal

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out of account, so that letter is dropped

blocks.clueFragment: Kemi’s possible statement of political allegiance
blocks.note: a Conservative might declare their colour: I'm blue
L is the abbreviation for Liberal; it is the letter removed

explanation.surface: Kemi's pledge of loyalty to her party is meant to inspire, leaving the Liberals out.
explanation.walkthrough: Kemi Badenoch leads Britain's Conservative Party, whose colour is blue, so she might say 'I'm blue'.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue someone with a feeling is to fill or inspire them with it.

clue.text: Spice Girls finally accompanying retiring singer in 1970s glam-rock band

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so just the last letter is kept
to retire is to draw back, so the letters run backwards
being in something means sitting inside it
one piece accompanying another goes along beside it

blocks.note: the last letter of Girls
an informer who sings to the police is a rat
Mud were a British glam-rock group with hits like Tiger Feet

explanation.surface: A Spice Girl sings alongside a retired vocalist from a seventies glam-rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spice Girls were a 1990s pop group, which is the surface trap; 'Spice' alone is the definition, and 'singer' is slang for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mustard is a pungent condiment made from ground seeds, a familiar kitchen spice.

clue.text: Sets out award after advancement of English vessels

indicators.note: advancing the letter for English moves it forward, so the final letter jumps to the front
one thing coming after another follows it in the line

blocks.note: the MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is an honour
arks are boats, as Noah's was

explanation.surface: An honour is handed out once English ships are promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: The MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire; its own final E is the English one that moves up.
explanation.definitionFit: To embark is to board a ship or begin a journey, so to set out.

clue.text: Spend penny, wipe surrounds

indicators.note: to surround something is to enclose it on all sides

blocks.note: p is the abbreviation for a penny
to wipe a file is to delete it

explanation.surface: Spend a penny, then wipe: a trip to the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spend a penny' is British slang for using the toilet, from the old coin-operated locks, which the surface plays on; 'Spend' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplete resources is to use them up, which is what spending money does.

clue.text: Closure of cricket grounds a serious offence

indicators.note: a closure is an ending, so only the final letter is taken

blocks.note: the final letter of cricket
the grounds for something are its reason

explanation.surface: Shutting down cricket grounds would be a grave crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds' looks like sports fields beside 'cricket' but means a reason or justification.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason, betraying one's country, is among the gravest crimes, historically punishable by death.
